title: Ban Krut, Bang Saphan & Koh Talu: 3-Day Trip Plan | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A 3-day, 2-night itinerary for the far south of Prachuap Khiri Khan, Thailand: Ban Krut beach, Wat Thang Sai, Mae Rampheung Beach, then a snorkeling boat trip to Koh Talu off Bang Saphan Noi, with piers, departure times, prices and real tips.

h1:
The far south of the province
Ban Krut–Bang Saphan–Koh Talu
intro: The far south of Prachuap Khiri Khan still doesn't get a big crowd, even though the beaches are long and quiet, the water is clear, there's a hilltop temple looking out over two bays, and Koh Talu, an island with healthy coral, sits just half an hour offshore by boat. This plan runs 3 days and 2 nights, easy to do in your own car, working south from Ban Krut down to Bang Saphan and finishing with a boat day out to Koh Talu off Bang Saphan Noi, complete with departure times, piers and prices we've checked for you.

blocks.html: Ban Krut and Bang Saphan sit at the far southern end of the province, about 1.5–2 hours south of Prachuap town and roughly 2.5–3 hours from Hua Hin. The sights are spread out in a long line along the coast, from Ban Krut Beach to Wat Thang Sai up on Khao Thong Chai, Mae Rampheung Beach in the Bang Saphan area, all the way down to the Koh Talu pier at Bang Saphan Noi. That's why this plan has you sleeping near Ban Krut for both nights and then driving south for day trips, so you don't have to pack up and switch hotels all the time.

blocks.title: Check the Koh Talu boat day first
blocks.html: Most Koh Talu boats run as a morning One Day Trip (boarding around 08:30, back ashore a little after noon) and need to be booked ahead. The sea is calmest and clearest roughly from February to May; during the monsoon the boats may not run at all. Call the operator to check before you lock in your travel dates, and schedule the Koh Talu day for the best-weather day of your trip.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Arrive in Ban Krut, walk the beach, then head up Wat Thang Sai for the view

items.activity: Arrive in Ban Krut, check in at a beachfront stay, drop your bags and find lunch
items.note: Ban Krut Beach is a long stretch of sand running about 12 km along the coastal road, and most places to stay sit right on the beach

items.activity: Have seafood at a beachfront restaurant in Ban Krut
items.note: This area has several seafood places and seaside cafes, such as Li's Restaurant and Krua Na Baan Hat Ban Krut

items.activity: Drive up to Wat Thang Sai to see Phra Mahathat Chedi Phakdi Prakat on Khao Thong Chai
items.note: The nine-tiered chedi stands on Khao Thong Chai, between Ban Krut Bay and Ban Thang Sai Bay. The temple is open roughly 08:00–16:30

items.activity: Walk around the chedi grounds and take in the view over both bays from up on the hill
items.note: Late afternoon the light softens and the bay views photograph well. The road up is paved, about 1 km, and you can drive all the way up

items.activity: Head back down for an evening stroll on Ban Krut Beach in the cool breeze, then find dinner
items.note: The beach is quiet and uncrowded, good for sitting and listening to the waves in the evening

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Down to Bang Saphan: Mae Rampheung Beach and fishing-village life

items.activity: Have breakfast at your stay, then drive south into Bang Saphan district
items.note: From Ban Krut down to Bang Saphan is about 30–40 minutes, passing Bang Saphan market on the way

items.activity: Head to Mae Rampheung Beach and walk the sand under the seaside pines
items.note: Mae Rampheung is a quiet stretch of beach, with rows of casuarina pines, mangroves, a canal mouth, and the fishermen's racks for drying fish and squid

items.activity: Have seafood at a restaurant on Mae Rampheung Beach
items.note: This area has fresh, reasonably priced seafood places such as Nok Kaeo Seafood, with ingredients straight off the local fishing boats

items.activity: Stop by Bang Saphan market or the fish-drying racks to see local fishing life
items.note: In the afternoon you'll often see villagers drying squid and salted fish; you can buy dried goods to take home

items.activity: Head back to rest around Ban Krut, or settle into a seaside cafe
items.note: Save your energy for the Koh Talu boat tomorrow, since it's an early start

items.activity: Find dinner around Ban Krut and get ready for an early night
items.note: Confirm your Koh Talu boat slot with the operator one more time, checking the meeting point and departure time

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Snorkeling boat trip to Koh Talu, then pack up and head home

items.activity: Leave Ban Krut and drive down to the pier at Bang Saphan Noi
items.note: Most Koh Talu boats leave from Laem Son Beach in Bang Saphan Noi district, about an hour's drive from Ban Krut, so allow time to make the morning slot

items.activity: Board the boat and head out from shore to Koh Talu
items.note: The ride from shore to the island is about 30 minutes (a speedboat is faster). A join-in group boat runs about 450–500 THB per person, less for small children

items.activity: Snorkel the coral at several spots around the island
items.note: Popular snorkeling spots include Hat Kruat, Ao Muk and Plai Hang, where you'll find coral, sea anemones and schools of colorful fish

items.activity: Step onto the island, walk the sandy beach and take photos before heading back
items.note: Koh Talu is quiet with clear water, and some tours include lunch or snacks on the boat

items.activity: The boat gets back to shore at Bang Saphan Noi
items.note: Rinse off and change at the pier, then find lunch in the town
If you're heading north back past Ban Krut–Bang Saphan, it's about 3 hours up to Hua Hin, and you can stop for souvenirs along the way

items: A car — public transport is scarce here and the sights are spread out, so driving your own or renting is by far the easiest way around
Book the Koh Talu boat ahead — boats only run in the morning and slots are limited, so always call to book and confirm a good-weather day
Water gear — swimwear, a sun shirt, reef-safe sunscreen, and a waterproof case for your phone
Sun and water — both the beaches and the boat are fully exposed, so bring a hat, sunglasses and drinking water
Cash — boat fares, local seafood places and many markets here mainly take cash

blocks.title: How to plan your days so the boat actually runs
blocks.html: The sea around Koh Talu is calmest from February to May. If you come at another time, set aside the Koh Talu day for whichever day the forecast looks best on your trip, and keep a backup plan on the mainland (Wat Thang Sai, Mae Rampheung Beach) in case the boat is cancelled at the last minute, so you don't waste the trip.

blocks.text: Extra stops if you have time to spare

items.name: Ban Thang Sai Bay
items.blurb: A small bay on the other side of Khao Thong Chai, just past Wat Thang Sai. The beach is quiet with few people, an easy add-on right after the temple.

items.name: Seaside cafes in Ban Krut
items.blurb: The Ban Krut area has several cafes right on the beach, perfect for sipping coffee and watching the sea in the morning or afternoon.

items.name: Bang Saphan market
items.blurb: The town market, with local snacks and dried seafood, an easy stop for souvenirs on your way down or back up.

faq.q: How many days do you need for Ban Krut–Bang Saphan–Koh Talu?
faq.a: If you want to take in Ban Krut Beach, Wat Thang Sai, Mae Rampheung Beach and the Koh Talu boat trip without rushing, 3 days and 2 nights is ideal: sleep near Ban Krut for both nights and drive out on day trips. If you have less time, 2 days and 1 night can work, but you'll have to choose between the Koh Talu boat trip and exploring on the mainland.

faq.q: Which pier does the Koh Talu boat leave from, what time, and how much?
faq.a: Most Koh Talu boats leave from Laem Son Beach in Bang Saphan Noi district. They run as a morning One Day Trip, departing around 08:30 and getting back to shore a little after noon. The ride from shore to the island takes about 30 minutes, and a join-in group boat costs roughly 450–500 THB per person, less for small children. Book ahead and check the boat schedule with the operator first.

faq.q: What time of year is best for Koh Talu?
faq.a: The sea is calmest and clearest roughly from February to May, which is the best time for snorkeling the coral. During the monsoon (around June to October) the wind and waves pick up and boats may not run, so always check the forecast and confirm the boat schedule before you travel.

faq.q: What time does Wat Thang Sai open, and is it hard to get up there?
faq.a: Wat Thang Sai, home of Phra Mahathat Chedi Phakdi Prakat, is open to visitors roughly 08:00–16:30. It sits on Khao Thong Chai, and the way up is a paved road about 1 km long, so you can drive all the way to the chedi grounds without hiking up the hill. It's a good late-afternoon stop, when the light is soft, for the view over both bays.

faq.q: How far are Ban Krut and Bang Saphan from Prachuap town and Hua Hin?
faq.a: Ban Krut and Bang Saphan are at the far southern end of the province, about 1.5–2 hours south of Prachuap town and roughly 2.5–3 hours from Hua Hin. The Koh Talu pier at Bang Saphan Noi is further south still, about an hour's drive from Ban Krut, so allow plenty of travel time.
